transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Thanks for making time, Marcus. I saw the Q1 earnings call mention about fraud detection lag — is that still the priority this quarter?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: It is. Right now transactions land in Postgres, Debezium pushes to MSK, and Databricks picks them up in micro-batches. End to end we're seeing twelve to fifteen minutes before a transaction is scoreable.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: And the fraud team needs what, seconds?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Shreya's team says anything under thirty seconds changes the game. Card-present fraud runs in bursts — by minute fifteen the burst is over and we've eaten the loss.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: That's the exact pattern we built for. Vector Pipeline sits on your Debezium stream and delivers enforced-schema events into Databricks in under a second. No changes to your dbt models downstream.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: What does the Databricks integration actually look like? Delta Live Tables? Structured streaming? We got burned by a vendor that claimed 'native integration' and shipped a JDBC connector.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Fair concern. I'll get you the integration architecture doc — it writes Delta directly, no JDBC. Can I also loop in a solutions engineer for a deeper session with your team?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Send the doc first. And I need pricing at fifty terabytes a month before I take anything to finance. We're a six-person data team; if this needs two engineers to babysit, it's a non-starter.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Understood — doc plus 50TB pricing, then a technical session if it holds up. I'll have both to you this week.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Works. Copy Shreya Patel on the follow-up; she owns the fraud models and she'll pressure-test your latency claims.

Intro call with Marisol Vega, who wrote the current mediation batch. Walked the CDR path: collectors → Amdocs mediation → Informatica → Exadata → Snowflake. Says the batch was sized for 2.6M subscribers and they are at 4.1M. Would not commit to anything without a parallel run.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Walk me through where a CDR actually goes today.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: Collectors at the edge write files. They land on a staging cluster, mediation rates and normalises them, Informatica moves the output to Exadata, and a nightly load lifts it into Snowflake. Four hops, three of which I own.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: And the batch was sized for a smaller subscriber base.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: It was sized in 2019. We have added a million and a half subscribers and a second brand since.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: What would make you believe a streaming path is safe?

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: Counts. If your numbers and my numbers agree to the cent across a month-end, I will believe you. Anything less than that is a demo.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: That is a fair bar. Who else has to be in the room?

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: Nadia. It is her budget and her risk. I am the person she asks whether it is real.

Working session with Nadia Kaur and two of her engineers on the mediation feed. Agreed the shape: Vector Pipeline reads the same collector output, runs in parallel with the nightly job for a full billing cycle, and nothing is cut over until counts reconcile to the cent. Nadia was explicit about timing — Meridian is in a change freeze for the Horizon cutover until 2026-09-08 and she does not want a proposal, a POC, or a security review started before then. She asked us to come back the week the freeze lifts with a scoped parallel-run plan for the mediation feed, including what her team would have to staff. Said Marisol Vega would be the technical reviewer.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Thanks for the two hours, Nadia. Before we get into the shape of it — is the batch still overrunning?

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: Twice a week, sometimes three. It starts at 01:15 and it is supposed to be done by 05:30. Hank's team needs it by six. When it slips, the day's revenue number goes out provisional and somebody writes an email about it.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: The window itself is not the problem. The problem is that the window was sized when we had 2.6 million subscribers.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: So the shape we would propose is: we read the same collector output you feed into mediation, stream it with schema enforcement into Snowflake, and run alongside the nightly job for a full billing cycle. Nothing gets cut over until your counts and ours reconcile.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: A full cycle. Not two weeks. I want to see it across a month-end close.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: That is the right shape. Now the part you are not going to like. We are in a change freeze until the Horizon cutover. Nothing new touches production, and that includes a POC in a lower environment, because my team's attention is the scarce thing, not the environment.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Until when?

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: The freeze lifts on the eighth of September. Come back to me that week. Not before — if you send me a proposal in August it will sit unread and it will make me think you were not listening.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Understood. What do you want in hand the week it lifts?

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: A scoped parallel-run plan for the mediation feed. What you need from us, what my team has to staff, how long the overlap runs, and what the exit criteria are. Marisol reviews it before I look at it.

transcript.speaker: Nadia Kaur
transcript.text: Do not start it. Imani's queue is full of Horizon vendors and getting in line early buys you nothing. September.

Number on file rings a decommissioned desk. (Stefan Kowalczyk)

Hank Delacroix sent his March-to-June overrun log: 31 late landings in four months, nine of them past 07:00. Said he would happily be quoted internally, and repeated that the budget for a fix is not his.

transcript.speaker: Hank Delacroix
transcript.text: Four months of data: thirty-one late landings, nine past seven in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: What happens downstream on one of the nine?

transcript.speaker: Hank Delacroix
transcript.text: The daily revenue number goes out marked provisional, my analysts reconcile counts by hand, and I write a paragraph explaining it. Every one of those paragraphs is identical.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Is that paragraph enough to fund a fix?

transcript.speaker: Hank Delacroix
transcript.text: Not out of my budget. Revenue assurance does not buy pipelines. Nadia's org does, and Nadia has a cutover to survive first.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Would you be quotable internally if she asked?

transcript.speaker: Hank Delacroix
transcript.text: Quote me all you like. Just do not make it look like I sent you, or the next conversation is about org charts instead of the batch.

Picked up between meetings. Not now, try after the cutover. (Oskar Lindberg)
Nolan Ferreira wants per-cell performance telemetry in minutes. He has a small tools budget of his own and could buy a narrow deployment without the committee, though it would not touch mediation.
Asked to be called back next quarter, no specific date. (Aditi Deshmukh)
Junie Alvarado retrains churn models on day-old features and called it 'yesterday's truth' in a talk last year. Interested, no authority, happy to be a reference internally.
No answer, no voicemail set up. (Roland Achebe)
Left voicemail referencing the nightly batch overrun. No callback. (Lucia Ferrari)

Marisol Vega pressure-tested the parallel-run idea: exactly-once semantics on CDR counts, what happens on collector replay, and who owns reconciliation during the overlap. Said she is fine being the technical reviewer when the freeze lifts, and that until then there is nothing to review.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: Exactly-once. Say the words and tell me what you actually do.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Idempotent writes keyed on the collector's record identifier, with a dedup window that covers a full replay day.

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: And if a collector replays four days because someone rebuilt a shelf?

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Then the window is too short and we would size it to your worst historical replay. What is that number?

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: Six days, once, in 2024. That is the answer I wanted — you asked instead of telling me it cannot happen.

transcript.speaker: Rep
transcript.text: Is there anything worth starting before September?

transcript.speaker: Marisol Vega
transcript.text: No. Nadia was clear and she is right. Write the plan, be specific about reconciliation ownership during the overlap, and send it when the freeze lifts.
